approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using accepted scores from the current objective session. It keeps the best 64 molecules for breeding and samples parents from high-scoring quantile bands. Fresh candidates come from connected fragments of two parents or successive local mutations of one parent, with bounded retries and saturation recovery. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities, duplicate rejection and a source-relative sulfur-signature gate govern admission to a surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete accepted archive uses integer-count Morgan fingerprints and count-Tanimoto similarity. Correlated posterior draws choose distinct pool members for evaluation; accepted feedback updates both the archive and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove ordinary connected-fragment crossover, sending every attempt through the inherited single-parent mutation walk while retaining its sampled continuation and saturation recovery. This tests crossover presence on the sulfur-gated composition. Earlier presence controls used Parents without that gate; completed siblings changed posterior components, pool breadth or ordinary continuation rather than removing crossover from this Parent. The real retained branch draw will expose when the original rule would have requested crossover, without constructing the omitted proposal. The predicted loss is a contribution test: a complete gain or no-material-effect result also answers the new question.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting uncertainty is the unisolated value of a heavily used proposal route on the actual sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180, not an established failure of crossover execution. All three actual Parent summary.json/run.log pairs are complete at 1500 calls per seed, with macro mean 0.59645311428869 and population SD 0.03397032998399878; seed macros are 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917. Its sulfur addition gained only 0.0007834645552323346 versus n-62daf219c70a, below the separate +0.002 endpoint goal. A read-only streaming audit of all fifteen actual Parent task logs, excluding emitted copies of breed provenance, counts 76081 multi-survivor breeding attempts, 34393 crossover requests, 29851 admitted crossover pool products and 1490 accepted crossover offspring. Of the accepted crossover offspring, 200 strictly beat their best generating parent and 753 later appear as actual breeding parents; the whole accepted panel has 648 strict parent beats. These adaptive cohorts establish use, not contribution, and crossover faces the better of two parents. The earlier exact removal n-767d2ce08797 on ungated n-62daf219c70a eliminated crossover from 73611 exposed attempts and lost paired mean 0.054937284705486644, with seed deltas -0.11291748433253601, -0.004694166605415995 and -0.04720020317850793, despite more parent beats and incumbent wins. Older n-1faebb978a01 lost 0.02886320397735261 under an exchange-containing Parent. These motivate a loss prediction but do not answer the new sulfur-gated applicability. The current Parent deco_hop seed-0 best-so-far jumps from 0.609560453893309 at evaluation 280 to 0.8561477222467935 at evaluation 281 through an accepted one-parent insert_atom product. This inherited realization stays in the complete endpoint panel; it cannot be assigned to crossover from its immediate route or discarded because removal changes the prior ancestry.

literature_review.conclusion: Conducted the two recorded searches and read the primary Mol GA paper, official repository README and actual crossover source. They support separating recombination presence from local mutation continuation and downstream selection, but provide no matched evidence of current sulfur-gated endpoint contribution. The useful direct prediction remains the actual historical campaign removals, with their changed applicability preserved. Register only the existing zero-probability removal, its passive real-draw exposure audit and the complete descriptive classification. A separate external model or replacement implementation is unnecessary. Attempts to open the Jensen publisher HTML/PDF returned 403, the PMC page returned a browser challenge and its old tagged repository was inaccessible; a guessed default_ga.py path returned 404. Those failed fetches add no evidence, and no result is invented or presented as a reused recorded node literature review.

sources.applicability: The generator family and quantile/greedy host apply, but the paper supplies no sulfur-gated count-GP crossover-only presence result. Its objective and budget differ from the current 300-observation final Top-1 panel. Adopt the component distinction and preserve the inherited protocol; do not transfer its reported performance or batch choice.
sources.finding: Sections 2 and 3 separate graph generation by mutation/recombination from population sampling and greedy survival. The reported Mol GA combines Graph GA operators with quantile parent selection, and its PMO experiments use 10000 evaluations and AUC Top-10; the paper changes generation size to five to permit more feedback iterations. This motivates keeping selection, survival and cadence fixed while testing one generating route, rather than inferring crossover redundancy from observed local wins.

sources.applicability: Use it as primary code evidence for the two-parent recombination principle and the need to audit actual construction provenance. No external code is imported or substituted. sources.finding: The inspected official implementation constructs recombinants from two supplied parents through non-ring or ring fragment cuts, sanitation and bounded attempts. It checks final identity against parental strings; its construction rules are separate from population selection and cannot be replaced by merely counting mutation wins. The live source also differs from the inherited Parent's single-bridge prefer-large/prefer-small construction.

finding_summary.headline: Crossover removal is fully exposed and lowers the matched mean by 0.043640 despite more local wins
finding_summary.insights:
Ordinary connected-fragment crossover has a positive conditional presence contribution on this sulfur-gated composition at the supplied descriptive scale. More local wins are insufficient evidence that the one-parent route substitutes for it: that route faces one parent rather than the crossover better-of-two hurdle, and its mean generating-parent hurdle was lower (0.419758 versus 0.455304 across the accepted streams). Gains were more frequent but smaller. Excluding the inherited decoration-hopping breakthrough cell only as a sensitivity check still leaves a mean loss of 0.029484, so that single cell is not the sole explanation. Two median_2 Child trajectories are byte-identical to earlier removal runs and add no independent historical realizations. This answers the new composition-specific presence question without changing the earlier controls or establishing transfer beyond these seeds.

Structural coverage also gives a mixed picture. Within-session typed core totals rose slightly from 1,847 to 1,867, while generic topology totals fell from 1,147 to 1,005; more accepted offspring were later drawn for breeding, yet accepted ancestry contained fewer descendant/source pairs. The Molecular assessment finds ring-rich output confined to 22-46 heavy atoms instead of the Parent 1-96 range, with no tiny fragments, but reactive attachments, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. These are observed output differences, not an identified explanation for the score loss. The result measures the whole adaptive rerouting effect, including changed graph RNG, pools, ancestry and future posterior inputs. Specific fragment value, BRICS compatibility, finishing, sulfur interaction and the mechanism of the endpoint loss remain open; higher-floor and numerical recovery were not naturally exercised.
finding_summary.results:
All 73,814 generation attempts used one scored parent and mutation, despite 33,358 natural opportunities for the original crossover rule. Every session was exposed. All 435 pools reached 160 members and all 4,350 emitted optimizer proposals were accepted; the sulfur, canonical-identity, posterior-choice and accepted-feedback audits reconciled.

The matched mean fell from 0.596453 to 0.552813, a loss of 0.043640 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro differences were -0.103844, -0.001329 and -0.025747. Nine of fifteen task/seed endpoints fell and six improved; four task means fell while median_2 rose by 0.001594. Population macro deviation fell from 0.033970 to 0.009762. Strict parent beats increased from 648 to 750 and sequential incumbent updates from 255 to 302, but mean positive parent-beating gain fell from 0.026623 to 0.021520 and total sequential gain across sessions fell from 5.819415 to 5.164818. The separate endpoint-gain requirement remains unmet.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families avoid tiny fragments, but reactive attachments, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: n-6059424cc614 produces aromatic amidines/amides, linked azaaryl dione systems, aryl-substituted aliphatic amines, quinoline/diaryl-ether nitrogen-carbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Rings and aromatic atoms are abundant: digest ring_closure_rate is 1.0 on every task, and aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.9966 to 1.0. These are molecule-level SMILES-text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Read-only RDKit perception of the accepted optimizer graphs gives 22-46 heavy atoms overall, versus 1-96 in the assigned Parent. All Child optimizer graphs carry rings; its output has none of the Parent tiny isolated fragments or largest aromatic concatenations. Distinct seed families and many changed ring cores support moderate diversity, but high-scoring series often remain close relatives with recurring peripheral substitutions. Recognizable amide, pyridyl, phenol, cyclic-amine, thioether, sulfoxide and sulfinamide chemistry coexists with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, peroxides, reactive acyl substitution, N-S-N cage segments and constrained unsaturation. These motifs require environment-specific assessment; their presence alone is not a measured synthesis, stability or toxicity result. Ring topology and missing stereochemical identity leave overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak despite some more conventional high-scoring molecules. The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 everywhere. RDKit FindMolChiralCenters with unassigned centres included finds at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 2590 of 4350 Child optimizer observations, versus 2455 Parent observations; these are observation counts, not unique molecule counts or proof of configurational stability. Neutral strings coexist with many potentially basic amines; charge-marker absence does not establish absent protonation. Digest charge incidence is zero except 0.0103 in the linked heterocyclic set. All fifteen brief-named Child and fifteen assigned published Parent trajectory files were present and read in full: each session has 300 records, comprising ten initial and 290 accepted optimizer observations, hence 900 records and 870 optimizer observations per task for each side. No trajectory, task or paired seed comparison is missing. context.comparison independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with no profile-mismatched seeds. None of the fifteen Child trajectory files is byte-identical to its assigned Parent file. The final digest excerpt is the late seed-2 batch, not the incumbent; all seed leaders and final batches were read separately. The Parent seed-0 deco_hop breakthrough at evaluation 281, score 0.8561477222467935, is retained as observed chemistry. Read through context.evidence_index, its complete trajectory is byte-identical in n-c55c3d520a2c, n-62daf219c70a, n-59c7b21b8199 and n-870ed6964d46, so those copies are one inherited realization, not independent supporting trials. Historical molecular gap wording was read in indexed n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a records and in the full assigned Parent assessment. Private graph descriptors and evidence locators are saved in .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r31-slot0-molecular/trajectory_chemistry_dossier.json. Only digest/authorized Child-trajectory SMILES are quoted in cited_smiles; Parent chemistry is described from its authoritative published trajectories. Rejected or unselected graph products, omitted recombinants, conformer energies, synthesis routes, and experimental chemical properties have no scored molecular comparison here. Chemistry-score associations do not identify component mediation or establish mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer molecules have 22-28 heavy atoms, with aromatic indole-like fused systems attached to aryl/azaaryl amides or amidines and methoxy, alkyl, thiol or methylthio substituents. Seed 0 favors an N-halo aryl amidine on a methoxy/methyl indole; seed 1 favors a vinyl-ether/methyl indole with an N-halo anilide. Seed 2 gives an ethyl/methylthio fused N/O-ring extension joined by an ordinary N-H amide to a pyridyl ring. These leaders have 24-25 heavy atoms, three perceived aromatic rings and three or four total rings. The seed-2 leader has more conventional local bonds than the N-halogen series, although its fused connectivity still needs synthesis assessment. Compared with the Parent, the broad compact aromatic/carbonyl family persists, but the Parent leaders include an N-hydroxy azaaryl amide and a pyridyl thiocarbonyl/carbonyl variant rather than these same seed families. The Child is not short of rings, amide/amidine nitrogen or aromatic acceptor centres.
liabilities: Direct N-Cl/N-F attachments, vinyl and halomethyl ethers, and occasional peroxides remain; halogen-string incidence is 0.8667. Carbon-bound aryl halogens and thioethers should be distinguished from heteroatom-halogen bonds.
Some late proposals add constrained cyclic cumulated double bonds or medium-ring closures. Ring digits and aromatic notation do not demonstrate an accessible conformation.
missing_features: More consistently conventional peripheral realizations of the favorable compact aromatic/amide or amidine arrangement are lacking among leaders, although the highest seed-2 N-H amides provide direct counterexamples to a universal reactive-bond requirement.

Functional arrangement is not reliably retained through ring and linker remodeling: similarly sized ring-rich proposals can lose the useful aromatic/amide organization. The trajectories supply no exact absent target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Seed-0 N-chloro amidine reaches 0.4163503402962837; several aryl/amide-nitrogen halogen substitutions tie at that value. Seed-1 N-chloro and N-fluoro anilides both score 0.4484138510190879. The two pyridyl-position seed-2 ordinary N-H amides both score 0.45555627303128626, demonstrating that N-halogen bonding is not required for the strongest observed label. In contrast, the seed-1 N-chloro amide with a nonaromatic seven-membered N-substituent scores 0.020787440458967972, and a partly saturated seven-membered fused-ring analogue in seed 0 scores 0.021623282473063696. A densely fused aromatic seed-2 proposal with six perceived aromatic rings scores only 0.07988723514484247. Thus intact compact aromatic/carbonyl organization associates with better labels; more aromatic rings or an amide alone does not suffice. The final seed-2 seven-membered pyridyl replacement scores 0.31128889452175423, below its earlier incumbent. Recorded Child/Parent best-observed values for seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.4163503402962837/0.4593573492521118; 0.4484138510190879/0.47411701813450596; 0.45555627303128626/0.4369542269692598. The visible gradient does not identify an exact missing target motif or prove a causal benefit from any peripheral substitution.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer molecules have 22-46 heavy atoms and retain linked aromatic/azaaryl regions with imine, dione, ether or anilino connections. Seed 0 develops a 34-heavy-atom fused azaaromatic/imidate-like ring system linked to a fluorinated azaaryl region; its leading allylic side chain carries no direct N/O-halogen bond or peroxide. Seed 1 expands to a 44-heavy-atom linked pyridyl/anilino/exocyclic-alkene dione framework with imines, N-Cl and many short alkyl branches. Seed 2 gives a 38-heavy-atom azaaryl/fused dione system bearing N-F, O-Cl, an organic peroxide and an allenic substituent. Leaders have three or four perceived aromatic rings. The Parent explores a broader size range and different linked families: its seed-0 compact fused carbonyl/thione azaheterocycle, seed-1 azaaryl ether/cyanate family, and seed-2 nitroso/small-ring family are all chemically different from this Child. Neither side has demonstrated synthetic routes for the unusual leading structures.
liabilities: N-halogen/O-halogen and organic peroxide bonding coexist in leading and final proposals. Organic peroxide incidence by RDKit O-O single-bond matching is 213 of 870 Child optimizer observations, versus 79 Parent observations.

N-chloro imines, exocyclic alkene-rich dione systems, halomethyl ethers and cyclic cumulenes require distinct stability and geometry assessment; the more conventional seed-0 peripheral chemistry is not proof of whole-molecule makeability.
missing_features: Stable alternative substitutions preserving the useful linked azaaryl/dione relationships are not consistently represented among the strongest labels. The high seed-0 family without N/O-halogen or peroxide bonds shows those attachments are not universally needed.

Independent plausible compact realizations of the successful linked heterocyclic arrangement remain incompletely explored; the published Parent family is available comparison evidence, not an exact missing benchmark answer.
Stereochemical and conformational definition is missing for fluorinated saturated centres and heavily connected variants; score ties do not establish equivalent chemical identities.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. Child seed 0 reaches 0.6143330571665286 with an allylic side chain and reaches the same label with an allenic replacement. Child seed 1 reaches 0.6275275735294118 with the expanded N-chloro/imine/dione family; Child seed 2 reaches 0.6173879243327287 with peroxide, O-Cl and N-F chemistry. Lower observations include the seed-2 chromenone/polyene/nitrile at 0.5153272576636289, a disrupted indole/anilide hydrazine framework at 0.5217864923747277, and a small-ring cyclic cumulene aryl dione at 0.5263435194942044. Labels associate with particular complete linked heterocyclic arrangements, while remaining insensitive to some peripheral changes and tolerating chemically problematic bonds. The final seed-2 batch continues the peroxide/O-Cl/N-F family; evaluation 300 scores 0.6166640798799731. Recorded Child/Parent best-observed values for seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.6143330571665286/0.8561477222467935; 0.6275275735294118/0.6204376881838878; 0.6173879243327287/0.6442339647723496. The Parent seed-0 0.8561477222467935 late breakthrough is retained without counting its byte-identical ancestors as separate discoveries. It contains its own O-F/halomethyl liabilities, so missing that family does not establish a specific synthesis-quality explanation for the endpoint difference.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer molecules have 25-44 heavy atoms, with aryl or biaryl regions joined to available aliphatic amines, phenols/ethers and cyclic or bridged nitrogen systems. The seed-0 29-heavy-atom leader has a phenyl-containing side chain, secondary amine, primary amino substituent, and difluoroaryl bridged nitrogen cage with four- and seven-membered closures. Seed 1 produces a 32-heavy-atom diaryl polyamine/sulfinamide with an aziridine and imine. Seed 2 gives a 36-heavy-atom diaryl-ether/sulfoxide/polyamine family with a substituted aminal-like five-membered nitrogen ring. Sulfinamides and sulfoxides are recognizable sulfur classes, not inherently invalid N-S or S=O bonding. Parent leaders instead include a bridged aryl tertiary amine, a diaryl diaza ring with methylthio substitution, and an unsaturated small nitrogen ring attached to a cyclic aryl ether. Both sides already contain many potentially basic nitrogen centres despite neutral charge notation.
liabilities: Strained aziridines, four-membered cage closures, substituted aminals and incompletely specified sulfoxide stereochemistry raise reactivity or synthetic questions; accepted valence alone resolves none of them.

Some proposals retain O-F, N-halogen or sulfur-halogen bonding, but the best recorded molecule has no sulfur or heteroatom-halogen bond. Aryl fluorination and useful ordinary sulfur groups should not be conflated with these liabilities.
missing_features: Defined stereochemical forms and conformations of the cyclic and bridged amines are absent: RDKit perceives unassigned tetrahedral centres in 868 of 870 optimizer observations, including all three seed leaders.

More consistently feasible local ring topologies preserving the aromatic/available-amine relationship remain unestablished. Aziridines, small cages and aminal environments need specific chemical assessment; none is automatically impossible.

A basic amine shortage is not supported. The missing capability is reliable chemical and stereochemical context around nitrogen centres already being generated, rather than adding a target-specific amine scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low seed-1 aromatic carboxylic-acid/amide/N-sulfonyl-ring proposals score 0.007354407913688945 and 0.008050370599396714. The Child seed-0 available-amine/diaryl cage reaches 0.9999873649964273, while a related alkenyl/aminal cage reaches 0.9972890479783548. Seed-1 aziridine/polyamine/sulfinamide reaches 0.9812710214745549, and seed-2 sulfoxide/aminal reaches 0.9731550514562216. Availability and placement of aliphatic amines with aromatic regions, rather than total nitrogen or sulfur count, is the visible association. The strongest twenty Child optimizer observations all lack direct N/O-halogen and peroxide bonds and carry nonamide aliphatic nitrogen; these examples show that reactive heteroatom-halogen chemistry is unnecessary at the strongest labels. A late seed-1 amide replacement still scores 0.9619010592903336; a larger seed-2 bridged-ether/aminal variant scores 0.8282981784171962 despite retaining several amines. Recorded Child/Parent best-observed values for seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.9999873649964273/0.9912539132815379; 0.9812710214745549/0.9999994532254913; 0.9731550514562216/0.9817975835038065. These labels do not measure affinity, selectivity, protonation or synthesis, and the aromatic-amine association identifies no particular docking interaction.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer molecules have 29-39 heavy atoms and combine aromatic or azaaromatic regions with nitrogen/carbonyl rings and N-methyl or short alkyl substituents. Seed 0 has a 32-heavy-atom diaryl ether/medium-ring system joined by an exocyclic alkene to an eight-membered cyclic urea/amine ring; both medium rings are perceived as eight-membered. Seed 1 reaches a 38-heavy-atom quinoline/biaryl-ether framework attached to an eleven-membered nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring carrying N-N and N-O single bonds. Seed 2 produces a 35-heavy-atom diaryl connected medium-ring dicarbonyl/polyamine family. Leaders carry two or three perceived aromatic rings and four or five rings overall. The Parent also generates quinoline-linked dicarbonyl and connected nitrogen rings, but its leading assemblies and ring closures differ. Familiar aromatic, amine, urea and carbonyl groups therefore coexist with challenging medium/macrocycle connectivity; the nitrogen/carbonyl content is not sparse.
liabilities: The strongest family includes N-N and N-O attachments and large nitrogen rings; these recognizable bond types require assessment in their complete environments rather than categorical rejection.

Cross-linked medium rings, constrained exocyclic alkenes and late peroxide substitutions create geometric or chemical questions. RDKit perceives at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 622 of 870 optimizer observations.
missing_features: Simpler or independently connected plausible realizations preserving the favorable aromatic, available-amine and carbonyl relationships are not consistently represented among leaders, although the useful N-N/N-O-free macrocycle is a counterexample to universal dependence on those bonds.

Stereochemical and conformational definition of saturated attachment centres and unsaturated medium rings remains absent. Synthetic access to an eleven-membered heterocycle is not demonstrated by its score.

Seed 1 reaches 0.24068866712572615 at evaluation 300 with its N-N/N-O eleven-membered ring; a related nine-membered N-N ring scores 0.23575954615657446, and an eleven-membered relative without those N-N/N-O attachments still scores 0.2328048313334737. These associations do not establish a required macrocycle size, N-N bond or exact missing target substructure.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer molecules have 26-32 heavy atoms, with fluorinated nitrogen-rich imino/carbonyl or dione heterocycles and substituted unsaturated rings. Seed 0 builds a 30-heavy-atom densely connected N-S-N/imine/carbonyl cage with a fluorinated cyclic ether substituent. Seed 1 reaches a 30-heavy-atom fused dione and eight-membered nitrogen-containing closure with an N-difluoroamino substituent and fluoromethyl ketone; a tied variant instead has N-fluoro/fluoromethyl amino substitution and an acyl fluoride. Seed 2 gives a 28-heavy-atom fused imino/carbonyl heterocycle with direct N-F, fluorocyclopropyl, fluorocyclopentadienyl and formate-ester regions. Leaders have four or six rings and two or three perceived aromatic rings. Later seed-2 chemistry includes fused unsaturated three/four-membered rings, thiols/thioethers and a nine-membered aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring. The Parent also has fluorinated imino/carbonyl leaders, but different large nitrogen-ring and small fused-ring arrangements. Valence-valid aromatic labels do not establish favorable ring geometry or plausible synthesis.
liabilities: Direct N-halogen/O-halogen bonding, acyl fluoride, formate esters, N-S-N cages and thiol-rich constrained rings coexist with familiar medicinal fragments. These are environment-specific liabilities, not a universal sulfur or fluorine defect.

missing_features: More consistently conventional nitrogen substitution and stable polar-region alternatives at the leading label are missing. Useful non-N/O-halogen examples exist, but the strongest labels still frequently include direct N-F or N-fluoroamino groups.

Geometrically credible alternatives to densely connected N-S-N cages, unsaturated fused three/four-membered rings and large aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings are not established. A saturated cyclopropyl group is chemically distinct from an unsaturated cyclopropene-containing fusion.
Defined stereochemistry and explicit assessment of imino/carbonyl tautomeric or conformational identity remain absent; the observed labels do not establish which state would be favored.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
